title: Programmable proteases designed to cut any chosen site

concept.text: Millennium Problems for Biology 8, Programmable proteases. Target: within 24 hours, design a protease that efficiently cleaves a blinded site in a folded protein in living cells; the full challenge is 20 preregistered sites at over 80% success; cleaving preregistered peptides in solution counts as partial success. Sources given: https://millenniumproblems.bio/.

change_log.change: Added by hand to BCH on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the twelve Millennium Problems for Biology (Sam Rodriques and Michaela Hinks, FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, 2026), each with a stated concrete target; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Programmable proteases
page.definition: Proteases, enzymes that cut peptide bonds, can be designed on demand for chosen sites in proteins inside living cells.

goal.need: A study published on 16 October 2017 used about 2,500 total generations of laboratory evolution across three trajectories to retarget a protease to interleukin-23, a human immune-signalling protein. Pretreating interleukin-23 with the evolved enzyme reduced its signalling in mouse spleen-cell cultures. This demonstrates catalytic control of protein function, obtained through a target-specific laboratory campaign.

statements.body: Westlake University and Westlake Laboratory of Life Sciences and Biomedicine
statements.quote: An enduring objective is therefore to create “molecular scalpels” whose cleavage site can be programmed at will

completion.title: Protease designs pass more than 80% of a 20-site blinded cellular challenge.
completion.criterion: For 20 preregistered, blinded, accessible sites in endogenous folded proteins, design within 24 hours of preregistration; demonstrate cellular cleavage at >80% of sites (at least 17). Catalytic efficiency and proteome-wide off-target cleavage must match or exceed widely used site-specific proteases. Subsequent laboratory work may only produce designed proteins for evaluation; screening and target-specific evolution are forbidden.
completion.basis: Problem 8's declared endpoint. Published design hit rates do not establish success across blinded targets.

milestones.title: A designed protease catalyses cleavage at its intended peptide bond in vitro.
milestones.criterion: Establish enzyme-dependent hydrolysis at the intended peptide bond and catalytic turnover on a chosen substrate. On 14 October 2026, Chen et al. reported activity in 36% of 135 zinc-protease designs; Choi et al. reported 13/69 active cysteine-protease designs. These are design hit rates, not success rates across blinded targets.
milestones.set_by: Protease-design research convention, exemplified by Chen et al. and Choi et al.; a qualitative catalytic-activity test without a shared numerical activity cutoff.
milestones.threshold_quote: catalyse cleavage of their cognate peptide substrates at the targeted scissile bond.

milestones.title: Designed proteases cleave preregistered peptides in solution while discriminating off-target sequences.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate efficient, specific cleavage of preregistered solution-phase peptides supplied with off-target sequences. Qu et al. reported cleavage at three chosen amyloid-β sites on 28 July 2026, with variable cross-reactivity; preregistration was not reported.
milestones.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific; Problem 8, partial success.
milestones.threshold_quote: specifically and efficiently cleave specific preregistered peptide sequences

milestones.title: One blinded cellular target passes the challenge's 24-hour design test.
milestones.criterion: Meet the completion criterion's per-site cellular and comparator conditions for one target. Choi et al.'s HeLa-cell result used a transfected reporter in three independent experiments; that reporter result does not establish cleavage of an endogenous target.
milestones.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific; Problem 8's per-site prerequisite.
milestones.threshold_quote: cleaves that site efficiently in living cells.

not_found: No public report of the 20-site blinded evaluation or the preregistered solution-phase partial-success test was located.
No comparator panel, numerical activity/off-target tolerances, or unambiguous off-target comparison direction is specified.
No numerical field-wide threshold for the initial laboratory demonstration was located in protease-design benchmarks, roadmaps or the cited papers.

results.finding: Of 135 designed metalloproteases tested, 36% cleaved their intended peptide bond.
results.detail: The paper also reports hydrolysis rate enhancement and a total-turnover experiment. The 36% is a design hit rate, not a success rate across blinded targets.
results.quote: Of 135 designs tested, 36% catalyse cleavage of their cognate peptide substrates at the targeted scissile bond.

results.finding: Designed protease PP507-S1 cleaved only its intended target among 3 Aβ-derived fusion substrates.
results.detail: The study also reported variable cross-reactivity among other designs. It did not report preregistration of the target peptides or off-target sequences.
results.quote:
PP507-S1  was  strictly  selective,
exclusively  cleaving  Substrate  1  (Supplementary  Fig.  S6b)

results.finding: Designed proteases cleaved targets in mammalian cells; the reporter assay used 3 independent experiments.
results.detail: The HeLa assay used a transfected reporter, not an established endogenous target. The text does not report a blinded target, a 24-hour design test, or the required per-site comparator conditions. The 24 hours refers to time after transfection.
results.quote: The designed proteases efficiently cleave their targets in mammalian cells, opening the door to a wide range of synthetic biology applications.
